requirement: Implement ConditionalRecordUpdater supporting update_records(df, filter_col, threshold, update_col, new_value, inplace=False) using .loc indexing, validating inputs, preventing unexpected caller DataFrame mutations when inplace=False, and verifying matching rows are updated while non-matching rows remain intact.
skeleton: Vectorized conditional DataFrame updates via .loc indexing preventing SettingWithCopyWarning and chained assignment drops.
caption: A numpy-backed module that ships its own minimal pandas-like layer and uses it to show a conditional update done with one indexer call instead of chained indexing. The Series wrapper copies its input array, supports boolean-mask reads and writes, comparison operators that return boolean mask Series, and copy. The _LocIndexer accepts a row mask plus a column name, raises KeyError for an unknown column, upcasts a numeric column to object when a non-number is assigned, and raises NotImplementedError for any single-key form. The DataFrame stores a dictionary of column arrays, exposes loc, supports deep copy, column and mask reads, and column assignment, raising NotImplementedError for non-string keys; a pd class namespace mirrors the familiar entry points. ConditionalRecordUpdater, with default_col status, provides update_records(df, filter_col, threshold, update_col, new_value, inplace=False): it raises TypeError when df is not a DataFrame, ValueError when filter_col or update_col is missing, and ValueError when threshold is negative. It works on df itself when inplace is True and on a deep copy otherwise, builds the mask filter_col greater than or equal to threshold so the boundary row is included, and assigns new_value through a single target.loc[mask, update_col] call before returning the target. The fixture asserts the inclusive threshold, the validation errors, and that the caller's frame is untouched when inplace is False.

rationale.teaches: Conditional DataFrame updates through .loc with a boolean mask, a non-negative threshold check, an inclusive comparison, and inplace=False by default so the caller's frame is untouched.
rationale.why: Chained indexing assignment emits a warning and updates a temporary copy, so the frame looks unchanged and no exception is raised. The fixture checks both the returned frame and the caller's original.

candidates.why_wrong: inplace defaults to True, so a caller who did not ask for mutation finds their DataFrame changed.
A negative threshold is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
The mask uses > instead of >=, so rows exactly at the threshold are not updated.
The mask is inverted to <, so the rows below the threshold are updated and the intended rows are left alone.
Chained indexing assigns into a temporary copy, so no row in the returned frame is updated.
